findings.reason: as written the section's gate measures nothing, and the case that would show the guard fires is one that composes while the lane holds and admits it, the shape §34's own done-when already uses.
findings.text: §35's two cases both "composes and completes a content review" directly, one with no plan-version meta and one whose version moves while it runs, but its own corpus singles out a different condition: of 473 composed plan-review deliveries, the 10 whose dispatch sidecar still reads `status: "lane-paused"` (composition held at the lane, later admitted through the queue) have 0 committed records under docs/state/reckon/reviews/plan/, while 456 of the 463 reading `status: "dispatched"` have one; both §35 instances are held ones (`dispatch.json` in .../a-limit-reset-reaches-every-session/r-20261021T143300022479-.../ and .../the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches/r-20261021T172514984517-.../ both carry "status": "lane-paused", "run_id": null) — so a test written to these cases would pass on the unfixed code and the negative control, which "restores the dropping behaviour the manifest identifies", could not redden it

findings.reason: an establishing worker sent to test a fix on the two named candidates would probe the plan's version handling and the plan's edit timing, neither of which the delivered/missing split implicates, and would miss the lane-paused sidecar that leaves a delivery naming no review run to be filed under.
findings.text: §35 offers "a missing plan-version" and "a plan edited while its review runs" as its candidates and rules out only the first, yet the property that separates its two instances from the 456 delivered-and-stored ones is neither: both instances were composed while the lane withheld and were admitted later, which is also where the section itself places the drop ("upstream of it, in how a delivery is found or settled")

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited report directory, its plan-review.json and dispatch.json, names_a_review_subject (reckon/crew/review.py:2019), _store_deliveries (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:2219), _index_append (reckon/ledger.py:2484) and the store field surfaced by reckon/crew/promotion.py (line 1629, emitted at 1736) all resolve; the committed tree docs/state/reckon/reviews/plan/<slug>/ exists as cited.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — both of §35's cases compose and complete a review directly, so neither exercises the held-composition-then-queued route; §35 (plan.html:294) carries the finding.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — logs are required under the run directory with a header naming revision and command and a closing EXIT= line, and the test runs in a temporary home, not a session scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — plan_review_store names what the field measures; no plan label, stage name or ticket number reaches a symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the two candidate causes §35 names are not the property its own two instances share in the corpus; the split is held composition, which both instances carry and neither done-when case reproduces.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one goal, "a review of an unversioned plan is stored, or says it was not", with the establish-and-repair chain and the plan_review_store receipt field serving it.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §35 declares no depends-on, informs or gates and needs none; its write paths (reckon/crew/promotion.py for the receipt field, the modules the manifest names, and the new test) do not collide with §36's promotion_checks.py.
